claims.claim: Montana starts enforcing Medicaid work requirements on October 1, while most states start January 1, and the early start is sowing confusion and anxiety.
claims.episode_span: Montana begins enforcing Medicaid work requirements on October 1.
claims.source_title: Montana starts enforcing Medicaid work requirements on Oct 1. Patients are confused
claims.supporting_quote: In most states, people with Medicaid coverage will have to prove they're working, volunteering or studying, starting Jan. 1. But Montana is starting that early, and it's sowing confusion and anxiety.

claims.claim: Ontario's $5 billion Protect Ontario account has spent $140 million.
claims.episode_span: Premier Doug Ford’s $5 billion Protect Ontario account has spent $140 million
claims.source_title: Ford government ‘Protect Ontario’ tariff program spent $140 million so far
claims.supporting_quote: Nearly two years into an escalating trade battle with the United States, the Ford government’s signature $5 billion ‘Protect Ontario’ account has spent just $140 million to shore up tariff-impacted businesses.

claims.claim: Deputy Minister Gadi Mayman said 36 applications totaled just under $100 million, 18 were approved for about $40 million, plus $100 million for Algoma Steel.
claims.episode_span: 36 applications totaling just under $100 million had been received, 18 had been approved for about $40 million
claims.source_title: Ford government ‘Protect Ontario’ tariff program spent $140 million so far
claims.supporting_quote: “Since the launch of the program, 36 applications have been received totaling just under $100 million,” said Deputy Minister of Finance Gadi Mayman told the committee.

claims.claim: Stephanie Bowman said $40 million is 0.01 per cent of GDP and the program is not working.
claims.episode_span: only $40 million had gone to help businesses — 0.01 per cent of provincial GDP
claims.source_title: Ford government ‘Protect Ontario’ tariff program spent $140 million so far
claims.supporting_quote: “Only $40 million in funding to help Ontario businesses. That’s 0.01 per cent of our GDP, so clearly the program is not working.”

claims.claim: Kenneth C. Griffin pledged $3 billion to Carnegie Mellon, described as the largest university gift ever, much of it for a Miami campus.
claims.episode_span: Kenneth C. Griffin pledged to give $3 billion to Carnegie Mellon University
claims.source_title: Donor Gives $3 Billion to Carnegie Mellon, the Largest University Gift Ever
claims.supporting_quote: Kenneth C. Griffin, the hedge fund executive, pledged to give $3 billion, much of it to build a campus in Miami.

claims.claim: Valar Atomics wants more than 450 reactors on more than 9,500 acres in Utah for a data center.
claims.episode_span: Valar Atomics wants to place over 450 reactors on more than 9,500 acres
claims.source_title: A startup wants to build a massive nuclear-powered data center on public land in Utah
claims.supporting_quote: Valar Atomics wants to place over 450 reactors on more than 9,500 acres in Utah to power a huge data center project.

claims.claim: Judge Kimya Holmes filed a police complaint against a CBS affiliate over reporting, invoking a law that no longer carries criminal penalties.
claims.episode_span: Kimya Holmes filed a police complaint against a CBS affiliate
claims.source_title: New Orleans judge files criminal case against CBS affiliate over reporting
claims.supporting_quote: A New Orleans state court judge filed a police complaint against a local CBS affiliate after it aired a segment scrutinizing a real-estate transaction in which she was involved, with the jurist invoking a section of law that no longer carries criminal penalties, according to the journalist who reported the story.

claims.claim: Public Citizen asked the FCC and FTC to stop three White House ads promoting Donald Trump; the White House calls them public service announcements.
claims.episode_span: Public Citizen asked the FCC and the FTC to stop three White House ads promoting Donald Trump
claims.source_title: Trump campaign ads paid with public money violate federal law, critics say
claims.supporting_quote: Public Citizen, an advocacy group, called on the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) and the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to intervene and block further airing of three ads it said were “designed to boost the image and character of Donald Trump”

claims.claim: Milwaukee agreed to a $575,000 settlement after 55 hoax swatting calls officials knew were hoaxes.
claims.episode_span: Milwaukee agreed to a $575,000 settlement after heavily armed police responses to 55 hoax 911 calls
claims.source_title: 55 Swatting Calls: A Couple’s Fight Against Online Stalkers and the Police
claims.supporting_quote: The city of Milwaukee agreed to a $575,000 settlement after months of heavily armed police responses to 911 calls to the couple’s home that officials knew were hoaxes.

claims.claim: The House passed the Ratepayer Protection Act 417-3, and Senator Jon Husted said it is the only bill with a chance to reach the president before the election.
claims.episode_span: the measure cleared the House 417-3 and is “the only bill that has a chance to get to the president’s desk before we get to the election.”
claims.source_title: The Senate’s last gasp before midterm elections
claims.supporting_quote: Husted called the bill, which cleared the House 417-3, the “only game in town” and tied its outlook directly to the upcoming elections.

claims.claim: Senator John Hickenlooper said House bills of this kind have no teeth and the Senate does not work that way.
claims.episode_span: in the House “it’s so easy and people go along with these symbolic things there that have no teeth,”
claims.source_title: The Senate’s last gasp before midterm elections
claims.supporting_quote: In the House, “it’s so easy and people go along with these symbolic things there that have no teeth,” Sen. John Hickenlooper (D-Colo.) said. “The Senate doesn’t work that way.”

claims.claim: A federal court ended the longest U.S. police monitoring, of Oakland, after 23 years, saying the department had mostly complied with a 2003 settlement.
claims.episode_span: ended federal oversight of the Oakland Police Department after 23 years
claims.source_title: Judge Ends Federal Oversight of Oakland Police After 23 Years
claims.supporting_quote: In ending the longest such monitoring in U.S. history, a federal court said the department had mostly complied with reforms mandated by a 2003 settlement after a police brutality lawsuit.
